meta.title: Scheduler and views
meta.description: The Scheduler component and its two views: what each one is for, how a reader switches, and what the two presets change.

basics.intro: Scheduler is the whole component: it reads the items, cuts the day into shifts, and renders one of two views. The list is for reading a shift from top to bottom; the timeline is for seeing how the hours are filled. Everything else on this site is a detail of one of those two.
basics.switch: The package does not draw a view switch — your page does, where it fits your layout. Pass defaultView to choose where a reader starts, or view with onViewChange to keep the choice in your own state, in a URL for instance, so a link opens the view it was shared from. The labels for such a control are in the locale pack, under views.list and views.timeline.
points: ListView and TimelineView are exported on their own, for a page that only ever wants one of them.
keepInactiveViewMounted keeps the other view mounted, so switching back is instant and its scroll position survives.
Below listOnlyBreakpoint the timeline is dropped entirely: a phone gets the list, whatever the view says.

presets.intro: A preset is the shape of the component, not its colors: the card layout, the strength of the level rail, how much air a row gets. 'default' is the one this site uses; 'classic' is denser and flatter. Both work in both color schemes and all three densities.

points: The component renders the active view only, so a keyboard never walks through a hidden one. With keepInactiveViewMounted the other view stays in the DOM, hidden, with every listener and timer paused.
A view switch is yours to build: a pair of buttons with aria-pressed reads well, and the labels are in the locale pack.
The component is one labelled region; its label is the schedule's name, so a screen reader can jump straight to it.
Heading levels inside it start at headingLevel, which defaults to 3: set it to fit the page it lives on.
slots and slotProps to replace or extend any part — see Slots and overrides.
classNames and unstyled to bring your own CSS entirely.
localization for every string the component shows — see Localization.
There are two views and no way to add a third. A different rendering is a job for <link to="/headless-api/">the headless API</link>, which gives you the same model without any markup.
The views cannot be shown side by side in one component; render two if you need that.

Switching views keeps the date and the pinned items. The scroll position of the view you left is kept only with keepInactiveViewMounted; otherwise the view you enter lands where landing.onViewEnter says.
